key_insight: Deep learning models can discover and generate functional internal ribosome entry sites (IRES) at scale, enabling programmable control of RNA translation; these designs are confirmed by high-throughput functional assays.
problem_solved: Lack of scalable, predictive methods to identify and design IRES elements for controllable translation, which limits rational engineering of RNA therapeutics and synthetic circuits.
method: Assemble large-scale candidate sequence library and measure translation activity using high-throughput functional assays.
Train deep learning models for sequence-to-function prediction and use generative models to design de novo IRES sequences with targeted activity.
Iteratively validate model predictions experimentally to refine designs and demonstrate controllable translation outcomes.
impact: Shows how generative and predictive ML can be tied directly to large-scale biological validation, providing a blueprint for sequence-level engineering tasks and closing the loop between model design and wet-lab testing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → deep learning predictor + generator → candidate designs → high-throughput experimental validation
Activity heatmap or scatter plot comparing predicted vs. measured translation for sequences (model performance visualization)
Motif/attention map highlighting learned sequence features or structural motifs that drive IRES function
Bar chart showing translation levels of designed IRES constructs vs. controls (experimental validation summary)
paper_title: Programmable RNA translation through deep learning-driven IRES discovery and de novo generation
paper_authors: Yanyi Chu, Di Yin, Dan Yu, Guangxue Xu, Junze Zhang
